title: Russia and Ukraine hold direct talks in Istanbul and agree 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner exchange
body:
On 16 May 2025, Russian and Ukrainian delegations met in Istanbul and agreed to a 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner of war exchange. Ukrainian Defense Minister Rustem Umerov announced the agreement, and Vladimir Medinsky, head of the Russian delegation, confirmed it to Russian state media. Umerov said Kyiv knew the date of the exchange but would not disclose it. Deputy Defense Intelligence Chief Vadym Skybytskyi said work on the lists of people to be exchanged would begin that day.

Ukraine's delegation was led by Umerov and included Presidential Office head Andriy Yermak and Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha. Russia's delegation was led by Medinsky, an aide to Vladimir Putin, and consisted of deputy ministers and lower-level aides, not senior officials such as Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.

President Volodymyr Zelensky had invited Putin to a face-to-face meeting in Turkey. Putin declined and sent Medinsky, and Zelensky called the Russian group a "sham delegation." Kyiv and its allies had urged Moscow to accept an unconditional ceasefire starting on 12 May, and Russia ignored the proposal. Ukraine hoped to discuss a truce in Istanbul, while Russia framed the meeting as a continuation of the 2022 talks and stressed addressing the "root causes" of the war.

The Ukrainian delegation met US officials, including Secretary of State Marco Rubio, earlier on 16 May. The previous prisoner swap, on 6 May, had returned 205 Ukrainian soldiers in a one-for-one exchange.
